encounter.notes: Winged vampire lord. Upright biped, NOT a low wide construct: the wings spread wide and rise ABOVE the horned head, so the top of the silhouette is wing, not head, and no scalar head_v_min can select the face. Pale flesh, horned skull, spiked pauldrons, red sigil loincloth, knee guards, clawed hands and feet.

reference.identity_note: The page is titled 'Vampire Lord' and was missed by an earlier title-only sweep; its BODY text states the model serves generic Gray Host Vampire Lords AND Lord Falgravn. Cross-checked against a UESP in-game shot: head plate, wings, pauldrons, sigil loincloth, knee guards and clawed feet all match.
reference.orientation_check: VERIFIED BY EYE before projecting, because this set was re-dropped once with front/back swapped. view-01 shows the face, chest sigil, forward-hanging loincloth and toes; view-03 shows no face, the spine and shoulder blades, the wing roots and the heels. Convention holds. Same pose in both plates - no pose mismatch. Re-checked by eye this session on plates/front-native.png and plates/back-native.png: front shows the face, chest sigil, forward loincloth and toes; back shows the spine, wing roots, rear tassets and heels.

geometry.provenance: Tencent Hunyuan3D-2mv (fp16, 50 steps, seed 12345) from the letterboxed view-01/view-03 plates (1311px square, full 884/1010px wingspan retained). Draft: 240,420 faces, 65.8s. HERO TRIANGLE BUDGET 70,000 (approved exception above the 20-50k standard): two thin wing membranes are the weakest case for marching-cubes reconstruction and leave few triangles per unit area at 45k.
geometry.budget_note: 70,000 chosen inside the approved 70-80k hero band, and NOT pushed higher: Olms showed 75,000 lands within 52KB of the 2.5MB gate for no measurable gain. Byte headroom beats triangles.

uv_density.note: Legacy scalar warp disabled; regions.boxes drives the density warp instead.

regions.note: No scalar head_v_min: the wing claws reach normalized y=1.0 while the horn tips stop at y=0.902, so the top of this silhouette is wing and a height threshold selects the wrong surface. Boxes measured on this mesh, NOT copied from Saint Olms - Falgravn is an upright biped whose wings separate from the body in BOTH x and z (at head height the wings sit at z 0.01-0.22 while the head sits at z 0.35-0.79), where Olms is a low wide construct. Verified visually on a membership render (build/lord-falgravn/box-check/sheet.png) BEFORE spending projection time: red claims the horns, cranium, face and neck; blue/green claim only the two membranes and their wing arms; torso, arms, loincloth and legs unclaimed. A first placement with y0=0.805 was rejected on that render - it took the horns and cranium but left the FACE grey, which no downstream metric would have reported. The pauldron spike tips take a weak partial weight; they are 96 vertices and adjacent to the head in the atlas anyway.
regions.targeting_rationale: Measured, not assumed - the boxes compete for one atlas. Sweep on the decimated mesh (unwrap + measure only, no projection): skull 4.0/wing 2.0 gave skull 246^2 front-facing and wings 159^2/159^2; 5.0/2.0 gave 265^2 and 150^2/151^2; 5.0/1.5 gave 287^2 and 125^2/126^2; 6.0/1.6 gave 300^2 and 114^2/116^2. Shipped 5.0/2.0/2.0. Olms deliberately targeted EQUAL texel squares (~200^2 each) because his skull was small and his membranes were 45% of the surface; Falgravn is an upright biped with a real FACE - eyes, brow, fangs - and his membranes are only ~20% of the mesh, so the correct bias here is toward the head. 5.0/2.0 clears the humanoid face>=256^2 bar at 265^2 for a 6% linear cost on each membrane, which carries only low-frequency veined skin. Do not read these as Olms numbers transferred; they were re-measured on this mesh.
